name: Credit spreads
summary: US high-yield spreads 3.30% on 11 Nov, below the 5 Nov one-year high of 3.48% and inside the 4% Watch line
state: The US high-yield option-adjusted spread was 3.30% on 11 Nov, down from its one-year high of 3.48% on 5 Nov but about 19bp wider than a month earlier (FRED). Both the level and the monthly change are well inside the 4% and 100bp Watch lines.
for_you: Riskier companies can still borrow at modest premiums, so there is no sign of a credit squeeze reaching businesses.
rubric_hit: HY OAS 3.3% below the 4% Watch line

sources.title: FRED — ICE BofA US High Yield OAS

why: High-yield spreads show how much lenders demand to fund weaker companies — an early warning of defaults and credit crunches.
drivers: Default expectations, risk appetite, rates, private-credit stress, fund outflows.

rubric.alert: HY OAS > 6.0%, or widened > 200bp in a month.
rubric.watch: HY OAS 4.0–6.0%, or widened > 100bp in a month.
